events.title: George Washington Inaugurated as First U.S. President
events.description: George Washington took the oath of office on the balcony of Federal Hall in New York City, becoming the first President of the United States under the new Constitution.
events.significance: Established the executive office and set many precedents for the American presidency and peaceful transfer of constitutional authority.

events.title: Louisiana Purchase Agreement Signed
events.description: The United States and France concluded the Louisiana Purchase treaty, under which the U.S. acquired about 828,000 square miles of territory for roughly 15 million dollars.
events.significance: Doubled the size of the United States, opened the way for westward expansion, and secured American control of the Mississippi River and New Orleans.

events.title: Death of Adolf Hitler
events.description: As Soviet forces closed in on the Reich Chancellery bunker in Berlin, Adolf Hitler died by suicide along with Eva Braun, whom he had married the day before.
events.significance: Marked the collapse of Nazi leadership and hastened the end of World War II in Europe, with Germany surrendering unconditionally in early May 1945.

events.title: Fall of Saigon
events.description: North Vietnamese forces captured Saigon, the capital of South Vietnam, and President Duong Van Minh announced an unconditional surrender, following the final evacuation of Americans and South Vietnamese allies.
events.significance: Ended the Vietnam War, led to the reunification of Vietnam under communist rule, and had lasting effects on U.S. foreign policy and on refugee migration.

events.title: CERN Places the World Wide Web in the Public Domain
events.description: CERN announced that the World Wide Web technology would be freely available to anyone, with no fees or royalties, releasing the underlying code into the public domain.
events.significance: Enabled the rapid, open growth of the Web, transforming communication, commerce, and access to information worldwide.
